style: Physical, set-piece-oriented All Whites built on a cohesive, hard-working defensive shape and direct play to a focal-point striker. Disciplined and well-drilled, relying on organisation and aerial threat to compete with stronger sides.
recent_form: Comfortable OFC qualifiers to reach the World Cup; enter the finals as the lowest-ranked nation in the 48-team field. Drawn in Group G with Belgium, Egypt and Iran.

key_players.name: Chris Wood
key_players.note: Nottingham Forest striker and New Zealand's all-time leading scorer; at 34 captains the side at likely his final World Cup as the central attacking outlet.

key_players.name: Tommy Smith
key_players.note: Experienced centre-back set to join Wood as the only NZ players to feature at two World Cups; leadership at the back.

key_players.name: Marko Stamenic
key_players.note: Young European-based midfielder providing energy and progression in the engine room.

historical_news: Enter the tournament as the lowest-ranked nation in the entire 48-team field (85th).
Chris Wood and Tommy Smith set to become the only New Zealanders to appear at two World Cups.
Drawn in Group G alongside Belgium, Egypt and Iran.

media_sentiment.label: neutral
media_sentiment.summary: Coverage centres on Chris Wood's leadership and a likely farewell tournament, with modest expectations given the lowest ranking in the field.
